q: The main object of inspecting suspense heads is to ensure that:

options.A: suspense totals match the budget estimates
options.B: no fictitious balance remains and old items are cleared promptly
options.C: suspense heads earn interest for the railway
options.D: all balances are transferred to capital at once

q: Age-wise analysis of suspense balances is primarily prepared to:

options.B: fix the number of suspense heads
options.C: identify long-outstanding items needing early clearance
options.D: compute interest due on suspense balances

q: An 'unlinked debit' in suspense accounts means:

options.A: a debit not yet matched with its corresponding credit
options.B: a debit supported by a paid voucher
options.D: a debit booked under the correct final head

q: The Suspense Register is maintained in the Accounts office to:

options.A: record all cash receipts of the division
options.D: watch the clearance of individual suspense items

q: Purchase suspense is debited when:

options.A: stores are issued to consuming departments
options.D: advance payment is made to a supplier before receipt of material

q: Purchase suspense is cleared on:

options.A: receipt and acceptance of the material with debit to stock
options.B: placing a repeat order on the firm

q: Long-outstanding debits under purchase suspense during inspection indicate:

options.C: advances still unadjusted though materials may have been received

q: Stock adjustment suspense is used for:

options.B: ledger and physical verification differences pending disposal

q: Manufacture suspense accumulates:

options.C: expenditure on jobs under manufacture pending allocation

q: Inspection of manufacture suspense should verify that completed jobs are:

options.A: charged to revenue a second time
options.B: promptly allocated to the proper works or stock heads

q: Suspense balances are generally reviewed by the Accounts officer:

options.B: only at the close of the financial year
options.D: at prescribed intervals, such as half-yearly

q: Items remaining uncleared in suspense beyond a reasonable period should be:

options.A: specially investigated and reported for early clearance

q: An unlinked credit under a suspense head denotes:

options.A: a credit awaiting matching debit particulars

q: Cheques and Bills suspense represents:

options.D: cheques issued but not yet encashed or paid

q: A credit balance appearing under a debit suspense head is:
Setting off debits of one suspense head against credits of another is:

options.C: not permissible; each head must be cleared separately

q: A suspense head should never be used:

options.B: as a parking place to avoid booking expenditure to final heads

q: Before closing the annual accounts, suspense items should be:

options.A: cleared to final heads as far as possible
options.B: carried forward exactly as they stand

q: Inspection should confirm that suspense schedules agree with:

options.D: the ledger balances in the trial balance

q: Old suspense items that cannot be cleared may be written off only with:

options.D: verbal orders of the dealing clerk

q: Sales suspense is operated when:

options.C: stores are sold on credit pending realization of sale proceeds

q: During inspection of sales suspense, the check is that:

options.A: the goods are put to re-auction
options.B: defaulting buyers are blacklisted at once
options.D: sale proceeds are realized and credited promptly, clearing the debit

q: Demands Recoverable suspense holds:

options.A: amounts due from outside parties pending recovery

q: An effective inspection of suspense includes:

options.B: verifying age analysis and action taken on old items

q: The executive department's role in suspense clearance is to:

options.A: ignore references from the Accounts office
options.D: furnish linking particulars and accept debits promptly

q: Unadjusted advance debits long outstanding in suspense may indicate:

options.B: advances not followed by receipt of stores or services

q: At the time of handing over charge, the Accounts officer should ensure that:

options.C: suspense schedules are current and old items are highlighted

q: Inspection notes on suspense heads require:

options.A: prompt compliance and reporting of clearance action
options.C: mere filing in the record room

q: A persistent adverse balance under a suspense head suggests:

options.B: misclassification or wrong adjustment needing correction

q: The certificate of genuineness of suspense balances is furnished:

options.C: by the Accounts officer after review

q: Suspense clearance drives are conducted to:

options.D: liquidate old outstanding items in a time-bound manner

q: Test check of individual suspense items during inspection should confirm that:

options.A: each item is supported by authority and linking particulars

q: Suspense relating to station outstandings arises when:

options.A: station balances remain unremitted or unadjusted
options.C: tickets are sold at the counter

q: Inspection of suspense heads forms part of:

options.B: internal check to prevent accumulation of unadjusted items

q: Items outstanding for over a year under suspense are generally:

options.C: reported to higher authority for special attention

q: Linkage of debits and credits in suspense should be done:

options.D: at the time of originating the entry with full particulars

q: If a suspense debit remains unlinked for long, the risk is that:

options.B: there is no risk at all
options.C: the amount may become irrecoverable or the transaction forgotten
options.D: interest will accrue to the railway

q: Sub-ledgers for each suspense head are maintained to:

options.A: track individual items and their clearance

q: Scrutiny of purchase suspense credits during inspection checks that:

options.B: material receipts are correctly linked and advances adjusted

q: A suspense head showing no movement for a long period indicates:

options.D: dormant items needing review and disposal

q: Clearance of suspense to the final head is effected through:
Inspection of Miscellaneous Advances suspense focuses on:

options.C: advances remaining unadjusted beyond the stipulated period

q: Unlinked items at the time of account closure should be:

options.B: carried forward with age analysis and vigorous follow-up

q: Inspection should verify that suspense debits are not:

options.A: merely parked to avoid showing expenditure under final heads

q: Age analysis of suspense balances is usually grouped as:
Suspense balances appear in:

options.D: the trial balance and balance sheet until cleared

q: A sudden spurt in suspense debits noticed during inspection may point to:

options.C: year-end rush of unallocated expenditure parked in suspense

q: Responsibility for acceptance of debits initially booked to suspense lies with:
Inspection of suspense heads helps detect:

options.A: frauds, misclassifications and delays in adjustment

q: Suspense items of inter-railway adjustments are cleared through:

options.C: acceptance by the other railway or accounting unit

q: During inspection, the examiner should see that credits in suspense are:

options.B: linked with corresponding debits and cleared

q: Adequate narration on suspense vouchers helps in:

options.D: easy linking and prompt clearance of items

q: Suspense review at headquarters level consolidates:

options.D: division-wise outstanding suspense positions for monitoring

q: If linking particulars are incomplete, the inspecting officer should:

options.A: call for the missing particulars and keep the item under watch

q: Scrutiny of stock suspense during inspection ensures that:

options.C: differences are investigated and not left pending indefinitely

q: Plus and minus balances under the same suspense head:

options.B: must be shown separately and each cleared on merit

q: Inspection of suspense heads is important because uncleared suspense:

options.C: distorts the true financial position and may conceal irregularities

q: A follow-up register for suspense inspection observations is maintained to:

options.B: ensure every observation is complied with and closed

q: Suspense items of closed works or completed transactions should be:

options.A: cleared without delay once final bills are settled
options.C: transferred to a new suspense head

q: A healthy suspense position at inspection is indicated by:

options.A: large balances over a year old
options.D: small current balances with prompt clearance and proper age analysis
